groups.name: Information-Theoretic and Computational Complexity Limits
groups.description: Risks arising from fundamental information-theoretic, encoding, dimensionality, and exponential-search bounds that constrain efficiency or feasibility of representation, transmission, learning, or search.

groups.name: Foundational Math, Modeling, and Cryptographic Risks
groups.description: Risks from misspecified mathematical/structural assumptions, abstract-algebra reasoning errors, instability of dynamical systems, and cryptographic vulnerabilities including quantum threats to public-key schemes.

groups.name: AI Corrigibility, Covert Capability, and Steganographic Channels
groups.description: Risks where AI systems undermine human oversight by disabling shutdown, accumulating takeover-relevant knowledge covertly, or developing hidden communication channels in their outputs.

groups.name: LLM Deployment Safety: Harmful Outputs, Jailbreaks, and PII/Copyright
groups.description: Risks from large language models in deployment producing harmful, offensive, or hallucinated content, leaking personal contact info or copyrighted text, or being coerced past safety filters via jailbreak prompts.

groups.name: AI-Driven Labor Displacement and Creative-Industry Disruption
groups.description: Risks from generative AI lowering creative-content production costs and displacing illustrators, designers, and other creative professionals from their labor markets.

groups.name: AI Second-Order Societal Externalities
groups.description: Risks from AI efficiency gains amplifying pre-existing harmful systems (factory farming, environmental load of compute, voice-assistant data monopolies, drone-based exploitation in low-infrastructure markets).

groups.name: AI Safety Community Operations, Outreach, and Research Direction
groups.description: Risks internal to the AI safety / EA community: misallocated research effort, fragile nonprofit operations, charitable-status erosion, brittle research infrastructure, and reputational damage from poor outreach.

groups.name: AI Governance, Longtermist Policy, and Impact-Market Integrity
groups.description: Risks in AI governance, multi-actor coordination, longtermist legal/policy structure (Windfall Clause, future-generations representation), unilateralist actions, short-termism, and impact-certificate fraud.

groups.name: NLP Reasoning, Multilinguality, and Cold-Start Capability Gaps
groups.description: Risks from NLP systems failing on multi-hop reasoning, lacking multilingual coverage, missing in-domain training data for intent detection, or imposing inefficient sequential search behavior on users.

groups.name: Hardware, Training Infrastructure, and Large-Model Scalability
groups.description: Risks from physical hardware design (chip placement, photonic routing) and ML training infrastructure: device memory, model parallelism, long-horizon memory, NAS collapse, VAE bound looseness, and dataset-in-graph memory blowups.

groups.name: Knowledge Graph, Ontology, and Symbolic-System Scalability
groups.description: Risks from prohibitive runtime, memory, and engineering cost of building or matching large heterogeneous ontologies and knowledge graphs, blocking timely updates in real-world domains.

groups.name: ML Evaluation, Reproducibility, and Distribution-Shift Methodology
groups.description: Risks from inconsistent benchmarking and methodology across ML evaluation, replication failures of public-facing scientific claims, and pretrain-to-finetune/deployment distribution mismatches that obscure true model behavior.

groups.name: Robotics Perception and Autonomy in Unstructured Environments
groups.description: Risks from robotic and embodied-agent failures driven by sensor noise, pose-estimation errors, GPS-denied navigation, and limited temporal memory for long-horizon physical action sequences.

groups.name: Cyber-Physical, Physical Security, and Adversarial Defender Strategy
groups.description: Risks where physical or cyber-physical adversaries exploit predictable defender schedules, malware obfuscation, uncertain adversary preferences, or unquantifiable cyber-loss distributions in critical infrastructure.

groups.name: Information System Performance, Legacy Code, and Cascading Failures
groups.description: Risks from poorly indexed databases, legacy mainframe codebases, proprietary IoT protocols hindering interoperability, overly permissive workflow models, and faults that cascade across shared service dependencies.

groups.name: Operations, Logistics, and Project Execution Inefficiency
groups.description: Risks from operational/logistics inefficiencies across construction, legal review, marketing funnels, air cargo, human-powered systems, project budgeting, and similar real-economy execution domains.

groups.name: Scientific Research Pace and Computational Bottlenecks
groups.description: Risks from slow scientific discovery rates: protein-structure determination, RNA inverse folding, qualitative-data analysis bottlenecks, and astrophysical mass-estimation errors propagating into theory tests.

groups.name: Human Cognitive Bias, Learning, and Assistive Technology
groups.description: Risks from systematic human cognitive biases (base-rate neglect, spatial-recall bias, dissociative misinterpretation), poor measurement of learning, distractive notifications, and burdensome recalibration in assistive devices for impaired users.

groups.name: Global Welfare, Public Health, and Diagnostic Pipelines
groups.description: Risks affecting human and animal welfare: child malaria mortality, wild-animal suffering, distributional inequity in development, urban displacement, unregulated brain stimulation, slide-imaging artifacts, AMD diagnosis delays, and inadequate flood warning.

groups.name: Geopolitical and Catastrophic Security Risks
groups.description: Risks of large-scale geopolitical or military destabilization: nuclear escalation, military-capability gaps, and erosion of undersea or strategic technological advantages by adversary state actors.

groups.name: Market Microstructure, Trading, and Metric-Driven Distortion
groups.description: Risks from market design and metric-driven distortion: thin liquidity in option chains and Goodharting in advertising-budget allocation that wastes resources by optimizing surrogates rather than true value.

groups.name: Civic Discourse, Democratic Erosion, and Collective Action
groups.description: Risks from polarization-driven democratic erosion, misaligned journalism on existential risk, and collective-action failures in high-stakes public-goods dilemmas such as climate inaction.

groups.name: AI Decision Accountability and Explanatory Burden
groups.description: Risks where high-stakes automated decisions lack contestability, where teacher-student or simulator agents develop human-uninterpretable strategies, and where exhaustive disclosure overwhelms supervisors instead of aiding oversight.

groups.name: Data Auditing, Provenance, and Analytical Interpretation
groups.description: Risks from missing or unreliable data provenance (timestamps, influence audits), oversimplified risk-communication graphics, and clustering output misaligned with analyst goals, leading to misleading conclusions.

parsed.notes: Of 131 residual risk nodes, 23 (17.6%) folded into HDBSCAN clusters (8 high-confidence with sim >= 0.72 and clear thematic match; 15 medium where the candidate was the best available but residual centroid distance >= 0.65), 107 (81.7%) seeded into 24 thematic groups, and 1 (0.8%) flagged as genuine residual (Stardew farming optimization, no thematic neighbors). Distribution skews toward broad cross-domain risk topics (welfare/health, cognitive bias, ops/logistics, hardware/training) reflecting that the residual is dominated by single-paper niche risks not deeply represented elsewhere in the corpus.
